questions.question: What is the name of the famous British social reformer known for founding the Indian Home Rule League in 1916?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annie Besant** was a prominent British social reformer, theosophist, and supporter of Indian self-rule.
 
• She founded the **Indian Home Rule League** in 1916 to promote self-governance and greater autonomy for India within the British Empire.
 
• Annie Besant was also known for her work in education and women's rights, and she played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Her efforts helped to galvanize support for the cause of Indian self-rule and set the stage for future leaders like Mahatma Gandhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annie Besant** was born on 1st October 1847 in London and became involved in various social and political causes throughout her life.
 
• She became the president of the **Theosophical Society** and moved to India, where she became deeply involved in Indian politics.
 
• The **Indian Home Rule League** aimed to achieve self-government for India through constitutional means and fostered a sense of national unity.
 
• In recognition of her contributions, she was elected as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
 
• Her legacy continues to be remembered in India for her contributions to social reform, education, and the independence movement.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India, announced the **Partition of Bengal** on **July 19, 1905**, and it was implemented on **October 16, 1905**.
 
• The partition was aimed at dividing Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam**, with a Muslim majority, and **West Bengal**, with a Hindu majority.
 
• The official reason given was to improve administrative efficiency in the large and populous Bengal province, which had a population of over 78 million at the time.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and marked the beginning of the **Swadeshi Movement** (1905-1911), a significant phase in India's struggle for independence.
 
• Due to severe opposition and unrest, the partition was annulled in **1911** by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**

 
 
• Launched in response to the Partition of Bengal, this movement emphasized the use of indigenous goods and boycotting British products.
 
• It saw the rise of nationalist leaders like **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**.
 
• Key cultural aspects, such as nationalistic songs like *"Vande Mataram,"* became symbols of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Challenges:**
 
 
• Bengal was the largest province in British India, making governance difficult, which was cited as the primary reason for partition.
 
• However, critics argued that the real motive was to create religious division and weaken the growing nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Reversal of Partition:**
 
 
• In 1911, the British annulled the partition due to the sustained opposition and shifted the capital of British India from **Calcutta to Delhi**.
 
• The annulment is considered a partial victory for Indian nationalists, though it did not eliminate British control.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Nationalism:**
 
 
• The partition and subsequent unrest significantly contributed to the growth of the Indian National Congress and the demand for **Swaraj (self-rule)**.
 
• It also led to the unification of Indian leaders across regions and religions to oppose British policies.

questions.question: The All-India Muslim League, popularly known as the Muslim League, was founded in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1906**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The All-India Muslim League**, popularly known as the Muslim League, was founded in **1906**.
 
• The Muslim League played a crucial role in Indian politics during the British Raj and was instrumental in the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
• The founding of the Muslim League marked the beginning of a significant movement for the political rights of Muslims in India.
 
• The party was established to address the concerns of the Muslim community and to promote their political interests.
 
• It served as a platform for articulating the demands and aspirations of Muslims, particularly in the context of the broader Indian nationalist movement.

• Its formation was influenced by a sense of insecurity among Muslims regarding their position in Indian society, especially in the face of the rising Indian National Congress.
 
• Key figures in the establishment of the Muslim League included Nawab Khwaja Salimullah, Aga Khan III, and other prominent Muslim leaders.
 
• Over time, the League's demand evolved from seeking separate electorates for Muslims to advocating for a separate nation, leading to the creation of Pakistan.
 
• The party's resolution for the creation of Pakistan was formalized in the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

questions.question: When and at which place did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?

__
 
• **The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, Punjab.**
 
• **It was a brutal incident where British troops fired on a crowd of unarmed Indian civilians who had gathered in Jallianwala Bagh to protest against the arrest and deportation of two national leaders.**
 
• **The firing lasted for about 10-15 minutes, killing and injuring hundreds of people.**
 
• **The incident had a profound impact on the** **Indian independence movement and is considered one of the darkest chapters in the history of British colonialism in India.**

__
 
• Morely-Minto Reforms__

 __
 
• The **Indian Councils Act 1909** was an act of the** British Parliament that introduced a few reforms in the legislative councils and increased the involvement of Indians (limited) in the governance of British India.**
 
• It was more commonly called the **Morley-Minto Reforms after the Secretary of State for India John Morley and the Viceroy of India, the 4th Earl of Minto.**
 
• The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces increased in size.
 
• Indians were given membership in the Imperial Legislative Council for the first time.
 
• **It introduced separate electorates for Muslims. **
 
• The members could discuss the budget and move resolutions.
 
• They could also discuss matters of public interest.
 
• They could also ask supplementary questions.
 
• No discussions on foreign policy or on relations with the princely states were permitted.
 
• **Lord Minto appointed (on much persuasion by Morley) Satyendra P Sinha as the first Indian member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.**
 
• Two Indians were nominated to the Council of the Secretary of State for Indian Affairs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Champaran Satyagraha was led by whom among the following freedom fighters of British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917, marking his first active involvement in the Indian independence movement.
 
• This movement was aimed at addressing the grievances of the indigo farmers in the Champaran district of Bihar against the oppressive plantation system.
 
• The success of the Champaran Satyagraha established Gandhi as a prominent leader and introduced the concept of **Satyagraha** (non-violent resistance) to the larger Indian populace.
 
• Gandhi’s efforts led to the formation of the Champaran Agrarian Committee, which ultimately resulted in the abolition of the exploitative tinkathia system, providing relief to the farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyagraha:**

 
 
• A non-violent method of protest developed by Mahatma Gandhi aimed at resisting oppression through civil disobedience and passive resistance.
 
• It is based on the principles of truth (Satya) and non-violence (Ahimsa).
 
• Gandhi employed Satyagraha in various movements, including the Kheda Satyagraha, Salt March, and Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Tinkathia System:**
 
 
• An oppressive plantation system under which farmers were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land, often one-third (teen katha) of their holdings.
 
• Indigo, being less profitable compared to other crops, brought economic hardships to the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Agrarian Committee:**
 
 
• Formed by the British government in response to Gandhi’s efforts during the Champaran Satyagraha.
 
• Gandhi was appointed as a member of this committee.
 
• The committee's recommendations led to the abolition of the tinkathia system and improved the conditions for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The movement marked the beginning of a new phase in the Indian independence struggle, where non-violent resistance became a powerful tool.
 
• It increased Gandhi’s influence and credibility among Indians and set a precedent for future movements.
 
• It highlighted the plight of farmers and brought agrarian issues to the forefront of the national struggle against British rule.

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the Champaran movement against the indigo planters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1917**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (2 October 1869 – 30 January 1948) was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist, who employed nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule, and in turn, inspired movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Champaran Satyagraha__: 

 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the first Satyagraha movement led by Gandhiji in India and is considered a historically important revolt in the Indian Independence Movement.
 
• It was a farmer's uprising that took place in the Champaran district of Bihar, India, during the British colonial period. The farmers were protesting against having to grow indigo with barely any payment for it.
 
• Champaran, where tens of thousands of landless serfs, indentured labourers, and poor farmers were forced to grow indigo and other cash crops instead of the food crops which were necessary for their survival.
 
• These goods were bought from the farmers at a very low price. Suppressed by the brutal militias of the landlords, they were given negligible compensation, leaving them in extreme poverty.
 
• Even in the painful time of devastating famine, the British government levied a heavy tax on them and insisted on increasing the rate.
 
• Without food and money, the situation was growing progressively unbearable and the peasants in Champaran revolted against the government in indigo plant cultivation in 1914 (at Pipra) and in 1916 at (Turkaulia).
 
• Raj Kumar Shukla who was an indigo cultivator persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to go to Champaran and hence, the Champaran Satyagraha began. Gandhiji arrived in Champaran on 10 April 1917 with a team of eminent lawyers i.e.Brajkishore Prasad, Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, and Acharya Kripalani.
